subject: Post-demo model shortlist — decision canvas and next steps
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Stiles <emma.stiles@novahealth.com>, NovaHealth Procurement <procurement@novahealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 4 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo model shortlist — decision canvas and next steps

Thanks again for meeting earlier — great first pass on the use case and the latency sensitivity (~95th <= 350ms) you called out. Per our demo and the perf runs we discussed, attached is a concise decision canvas and a recommended 3-model shortlist that balances cost / latency / quality for your triage+summarization workflow. High level:

- Recommendation (shortlist):
  1) Redwood-Serve-Medium-q4 (quantized) — balanced cost (~$0.0009/token), median latency ~120ms on our dedicated GPU profile, best-in-class instruction-following on out-of-domain clinical notes; slight drop on very-long-context edge cases.
  2) OpenFlare-XL (8-bit) — stronger factuality on knowledge-heavy prompts, higher cost (~$0.0016/token) and median latency ~200ms; good fallback for high-precision paths.
  3) RDX-96Q (int8-optimized) — lowest unit cost (~$0.0006/token) and excellent throughput for batch jobs, but we observed a 4–6% lift in hallucinations on free-form summarization.

Attached: nova_prism_benchmarks_v1.csv (benchmarks used for numbers) and prompt_set_v1.md (seed prompts we ran). Also linking the Drive folder with raw traces and the HubSpot deal.

Proposed next steps (mutual action plan):
- NovaHealth: confirm the evaluation sprint scope (subset of 2k anonymized notes + 200 user scenarios) and compliance asks (PII redaction expectations).
- Redwood: provide an evaluation image with the three shortlisted models, the prompt pack, and a small regression-check harness (we'll ship as a container).
- Timing: target 2-week eval starting week of 10 May; we can start earlier if procurement confirms the pilot terms.

Criteria we suggest for the sprint: ROUGE-L/ROUGE-1, factuality checks (precision@k against gold facts), 95th latency under 350ms for at least one candidate in the pairwise test, and a regression guardrail (no model should increase hallucination score by >2% vs baseline).

Can you confirm (a) scope and (b) whether procurement needs a formal SOW before we hand over the image?

Thanks,
Olga Petrov
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
olga.petrov@redwood.ai
Redwood Inference

Thanks Olga — helpful canvas and clear asks. A couple quick points from our side:

- Scope: the 2k anonymized notes + 200 scenarios sounds right. We'll redacted PHI before sending, but can you confirm Redwood's recommended redaction checklist so we don't miss anything?
- Latency: our internal bar is actually 95th <= 300ms for interactive flows. Can any of the shortlisted models run under that consistently for single-request low-burst traffic?
- Procurement: they will likely ask for SOC2 and a short pilot amendment rather than a full SOW. I looped them in.

Also, are there any specific prompt engineering recommendations you saw in the demo that improved factuality? Emma

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 5 May 2027 08:50:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo model shortlist — tech notes and evaluation plan

Olga / Ben — quick technical addendum that I recommend we paste into the evaluation playbook we send to NovaHealth:

1) Quantization caveats: Redwood-Serve-Medium-q4 shows best latency vs cost because of our kernel fusion for q4, but for long-context (>2,048 tokens) you may see KV-cache pressure that increases 95th latency. For the interactive bar (95th <= 300ms) we expect: Redwood-Serve-Medium-q4 (single request) median 110ms / 95th ~250-280ms on a c6-gpu instance; OpenFlare-XL median 180ms / 95th ~320ms (may not meet 300ms SLO in worst case), RDX-96Q median 140ms / 95th ~310ms.

2) Prompt engineering levers that helped on demo: explicit task framing ("Extract 3 facts and cite evidence with offsets"), short system-level priming, and a 2-turn safety guardrail that rejects hallucination-prone asks. We included a prompt_set_v1.md with the seed templates. Recommend NovaHealth run a 1k prompt sweep with different temperature/top-p bands and a toxicity/factuality filter.

3) Regression/watchdog: we will run a diff test against your provided golden set and produce a simple regression dashboard (delta in factuality, ROUGE-L, and token cost). If any candidate exceeds the hallucination delta threshold (>2% false-positive facts), we flag for manual review.

4) Data handling: we will not persist raw notes in hosted logs by default for the pilot; if NovaHealth prefers a private deployment image we can offer a VPC/private package for the pilot (that will impact timeline and procurement).

I'll attach the CSV with the bench traces and the initial prompt pack in the follow-up email to the external thread.

—Karthik
Staff ML Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.ai

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Post-demo model shortlist — decision canvas and next steps

Emma — appreciate the quick clarifications. Short answers and proposed concrete steps below.

- Redaction checklist: attached to Drive (short doc in the folder) — please run PHI redaction and share the anonymized bundle (S3 link or Drive) by EOD 7 May. We recommend removing direct identifiers and tokenizing dates; we can also accept a hashed-id map if you need traceability.
- Latency SLO: Karthik's numbers above reflect single-request performance on our dedicated instance profiles. Redwood-Serve-Medium-q4 is the only candidate that reliably meets your 95th <= 300ms target in our tests; OpenFlare-XL is borderline in worst-case. We'll highlight this in the evaluation brief.
- Pilot terms / procurement: Ben has proposed a 30-day pilot amendment with a $5k cap and a 10% credit; we'll attach SOC2 evidence and a short tech-sheet to the HubSpot deal. Procurement — please let us know if you prefer an amendment or a PO-first flow and we'll route legal.

Proposed kickoff & timeline:
- 7 May: NovaHealth shares anonymized dataset + success criteria confirmation.
- 10 May: Redwood provides evaluation container (three models + harness) and prompt pack.
- 10–24 May: 2-week evaluation window (we'll run nightly regression diffs and a final report).
- 25 May: 30–45 minute review + next steps (commercial and deployment options).

If that looks good, can procurement confirm the pilot amendment path and Emma confirm the dataset delivery by tomorrow EOD? I'd like to lock the 10 May start so engineering has time to stage the image.

Thanks,
Olga Petrov
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
